main_text.p: agitatione humor, illorum receptaculum, non poteft non diftendi, acres enim illæ particulæ vehementius circumactæ, majorem locum exigunt, quàm si essent magis quietæ. Etenim subtilis materia arctiora interstitia, quæ inter humorum particulas acidas & salsas sibi permixtas reperiuntur, facilius transiens particulas illas acres heterogeneas, & diverso situ sese mutuò respicientes, tumultuario quodam motu intestino diversimodè agitat: particulæ verò illein orbem actemajorem locum occupantes, quàm cum quiescerent, humores distendunt imò vehementius actæ flatuum bullarumve in ebulliente illo humore contentarum, atque præternaturalis humorum illorum distensionis, sæpius memoratæ, causæ sunt: humor itaque ille ex humoribus diversâ acredine constantibus & vehementer actis compositus effervescit, attollitur, turget, id est, μετεωρίζεται[?] [illegible, ~4 letters], uti ex fundamentis à Cartesio diligen-

page.notes: The left edge of the scan is cropped, so the first letters of many lines are cut off; these are given as the printed fragments. The Greek words at the end of the penultimate line are only partly legible; the first is read as μετεωρίζεται with doubt, and the second word is illegible. The line-initial fragments (e.g. "lum", "enim", "subtilis") are kept as they stand on the scan.
